analysis: The only change to docs/architecture/inference.md is documentation. The date line 3 moves from 2026-10-30 to 2026-10-31. The `stop` row of the request-parameter table (around line 2122) is reworded to say that Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans per request through `ReasoningStopScope`, and that the native block engine matches the whole output. The supplied units are the base excerpt (lines 5323-5378, Qwen27 TP MTP and capacity text) and the head excerpt (lines 1-419). Neither excerpt contains the changed table row, so I judged the stop-scope change only from the patch excerpt. No code, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption, prefix-cache storage, coordinator-provider protocol or fan-helper behavior changes in this PR. No threat-model assets, boundaries or mitigations (T-041, TB-002, TB-007 and others) are weakened or invalidated. The new text describes stop-sequence matching scope. That is an output-formatting and parsing behavior and not a trust-boundary change. Whether the code actually implements ReasoningStopScope as described, and whether stop-string handling inside reasoning spans could leak or alter content, is outside the supplied evidence. The code itself is not in this PR, so I cannot verify it, and a documentation edit does not show a regression. The surrounding text I examined adds no new attack surface. It covers the cluster setup, Nemotron Super video and image decode bounds, and TP MTP cohort arithmetic. All of that is unchanged context. I have no concern that needs deeper review.
